name: log-viewer
purpose: Composition-based terminal log viewer for CI/deploy output. **LogViewer** is the root shell and context provider; **`LogViewer.Header`**, **`LogViewer.Content`**, and **`LogViewer.Footer`** are composed as children so teams can reorder, omit, or replace the toolbar and footer without forking the log renderer. **`LogViewer.Steps`** shows a run with known steps (build, deploy, provisioning) as a pipeline: one collapsible step per phase, each with its own log, a Phased or Complete switch and an optional flush progress bar. Use LogViewer for build, deploy or runtime log lines, and LogViewer.Steps when the run has named steps; for code the person reads or copies use CodeBlock, and for code the person edits use CodeEditor.
useWhen: Showing build, deploy or CI output as timestamped lines the reader can search, filter to warnings, and copy.
A log shell whose toolbar and footer vary by screen — compose `LogViewerHeader`, `LogViewerContent` and `LogViewerFooter` in the order you need, or drop the ones you don't.

A run log with levels (`debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error`), such as what a function printed during a test run: set `level` on each line and `levels` on the root, and the header filters by level with a count per level.
A log that is still loading from the server — set `loading` to show a spinner and `loading-label` in place of the body.
A build or deploy run with known steps → `LogViewer.Steps` with one entry per step; every deploy-log block composes it instead of rebuilding the pipeline.
avoidWhen: Static, read-only code or configuration snippets → use `code-block`.
An animated terminal session on a marketing page → use `cli-terminal-section`.
Rows of structured records with columns, sorting or paging → use `table`.
The steps of a form or setup the person moves through (no log under each step) → use `stepper`.
The timed spans of one request or invocation → use `trace`.
related: `code-block` — highlighted source code with a copy action, not a stream of typed log lines.
`cli-terminal-section` — marketing band that plays a scripted terminal session.
`stepper` — the steps of a wizard the person moves through; `LogViewer.Steps` is the steps of a run that a machine moves through, each with its log.
`trace` — the spans of one request on a time axis, not log lines.
`create/create-deploy-success` — the post-deploy screen that embeds `log-viewer` for the build log.
bestPractices: Give every line a stable `id` and a `type` (`text`, `folder`, `framework-version`, `success`); the type drives the line's rendering. A warning is a `text` line with `level: 'warn'`; `level` drives the level toggles; the `warn` toggle is the warnings shortcut.

For a run log, give each line a `level` and put the run offset (`120 ms`, `1.24 s`) in `time`; pass the levels the run can print as `levels` so every level is offered even when it has no line yet. Bind `v-model:level` when the app needs the chosen level.
Bind `v-model:search` and `v-model:level` when the app needs the filter state; otherwise leave them unbound and the header manages them.
Set `:bordered="false"` when the log sits inside a surface that already frames it (an accordion panel, a drawer).
The copy control hides while `disabled` or `loading`, or when there is nothing to copy; listen to `@copy` for the copied text instead of reading the clipboard.
Use the header's `start` / `end` / `search` slots and the footer's default slot to add actions, rather than rebuilding the toolbar.

props.name: lines
props.doc: Log entries; filtered in LogViewerContent by search and level.

props.name: bordered
props.doc: Draw the outer card border and corner radius around the log shell. On by default; set `:bordered="false"` to render the shell flush inside a surface that already frames it (an accordion panel, a drawer). Internal dividers (header/footer edges) are unaffected.

props.name: searchPlaceholder
props.doc: Placeholder for the default header search field. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Find in logs`).

props.name: copyable
props.doc: Shows the copy-to-clipboard control (a CopyButton pinned top-right over the log content in LogViewerContent).

props.name: loading
props.doc: Replaces the LogViewerContent log body with a centered spinner and label.

props.name: loadingLabel
props.doc: Label shown beneath the spinner while `loading`. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Loading…`).

props.name: levels
props.doc: Levels the header offers as filter toggles, each with its line count; a level with no line is still offered. Empty hides the level filter.

props.name: error
props.doc: Message shown in place of the log body when the log failed to load. Empty shows the log.

events.name: copy
events.notes: Fires after a successful copy; payload is the copied plain text.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: Sub-components (LogViewerHeader, LogViewerContent, LogViewerFooter) composed in the desired order.
